issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds D^\alpha I(F_{k+1}(v_{k+1}^h)) by C\Delta t times only the nodal derivative sum, omitting the additive 1 in Assumption 4.1(iii). If f=0 and F(t,x,0,0,0)\neq0, then M_n=\max_{|\alpha|\le3}\sup|D^\alpha v^h(t_n,\cdot)|=0, while one backward step generally gives a nonzero O(\Delta t) interpolant; thus the recursion M_k\le(1+C\Delta t)M_{k+1} is not justified as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound \max_j|F_{k+1,j}| by C(1+\max_{|\beta|\le2}|D^\beta v^h(t_{k+1},x^j)|), giving M_k\le(1+C\Delta t)M_{k+1}+C\Delta t, and close by backward induction using \Delta t\le T.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform C_1 bounds and the time-Lipschitz bound in Lemma 4.9 are not established by the stated induction, so the boundedness/equicontinuity input used in the proof of Theorem 4.5 is unsupported until the induction is repaired.
issues.title: Stability induction drops the additive constant in the linear growth bound
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local added constant plus the standard backward-induction/Gronwall step; the claimed C_1 bounds, the later use in Theorem 4.5, and all rates survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate is claimed on the hypercube (-R,R)^d, but the cutoff satisfies \zeta(x/R)=1 only when |x|\le R. For d\ge2 the cube contains points with |x|>R, e.g. (0.9R,0.9R) in dimension 2, so \tilde u^\varepsilon(x) need not equal u^\varepsilon(x) and the displayed equality is unjustified there.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose \zeta to equal 1 on \{|x|\le\sqrt d\} (equivalently on the scaled cube) and to vanish outside \{|x|\le\sqrt d+c\}; the support volume is still O(R^d), so the H^\kappa bound C\varepsilon^{-\kappa}R^{d/2} and the final minimized rate are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 4.10 is not proved on the whole stated domain; the uses of this lemma in Theorem 4.5 for J_m\to0 and for terminal interpolation are therefore unsupported as written.
issues.title: Cutoff in the Lipschitz interpolation error proof is one on a ball, not on the cube
issues.why_classification: Only the cutoff radius has to be enlarged from 1 to \sqrt d; this is a contained local repair that preserves the statement, the exponent (2\tau+1)/(2+2\kappa), the R-power, and the downstream use in Theorem 4.5.
